title: Out of Life
essence: A dim high-rise bedroom where a man reads a poem to a back that will not turn around: the EX on the fire escape, vaping, while the haze eats the room left to right and the window slides away from every step toward it. Then two bodies fall past streaking towers with a gap between them that breathes and never closes, through a slow-motion vintage party and a hole in its floor, until the only light left in the film is the vape ember, a blue speck on black.
palette_notes: Night blacks and wet teal come from Naraka stills 22ddf809 (blue vapour bloom over a lit shopfront) and 62b9740c (flooded tunnel, cold light at the end); the steel greys and lit window specks from the hive fall shot 8519865f. The warm amber/gold pair (#c9873a, #e9b46a) is the vintage party's light leaks (a883ad75) and the bedroom's one lamp. #5aa7ff is the suite accent and in this poem it belongs to the vape ember alone: the last light in the film. #2a1a2e is the plum of the party's darks so the ballroom does not go brown.

full_text.line: What we've made we don't want, what we've sold to the world, to ourselves, doesn't exist.
I look for a way out through the hallways, within the drawers and fire escapes, trip
on my own words, falling out of life, and find where you go when you leave.
It was the maze constructed by a tainted love, a known yet unknown pit beneath the quicksands
of the make-believe haven, and hidden in the overnourished forest of escapism that calls
At this age, I'll follow, following the full distance between us almost having it all and
starting anew, to rediscover when love was real.
I failed at protecting you from your own vices, crashing the party of your evilest instincts
to find vibrations that echo in silence, love and hate languages that translate and slow
dripping blood salivating on imminent doubts, fully awakening to our darkest nights.
Pause for a second, a spectrum of fields will thread needles of garments made of sweet memories
and photographs, film and fiction that leave me empty.
With your back faced against me, you offer me a new pursuit of happiness as I stumble
on my own words, landing into the secret of where you go when you leave, and I fall

best_footage.element: a lone figure at a rooftop rail, back to camera, city haze beyond, wet concrete with a red reflection
best_footage.why: this is the EX exactly: broad back at a rail, face never shown, exhaling into a teal city. Lift the rail height, the figure's scale against the skyline and the red glint on the wet floor for the fire-escape landing.

best_footage.element: a blue vapour bloom rolling across a lit shopfront, lanterns glowing through it
best_footage.why: the vape haze reference: dense, cold blue, lit from inside by warm lamps. Cut the haze cards from its silhouette: billowing tops, flat bottoms, three layers of density.

best_footage.element: worm's-eye between converging tower faces, scattered lit windows, a pale hole of sky
best_footage.why: the fall void. Turn it 180 degrees and the towers become the slabs that streak upward past the fallers; the lit-window pattern is the paint spec for the tower strips.

best_footage.element: motion-blurred dancers, pink and amber light leaks, haze over a crowd
best_footage.why: the vintage party's euphoric light: copy the warm leak gradient onto a gel card over the ballroom and paint the extras soft-edged so they read as slow motion against POET's hard ink edge.

best_footage.element: a flooded corridor of stacked crates with one cold light at the vanishing point
best_footage.why: the hallway maze: a corridor that only promises an exit. Its vanishing light is the 'far door of the maze' the world module keeps moving.

best_footage.element: black-and-white stairwell with a steel handrail and smoke in the shaft
best_footage.why: the fire-escape railing and stair profile in silhouette; its grey value range is what the fire escape should be when the haze has taken the colour out.

best_footage.element: fog-drowned high-rises with a few warm windows
best_footage.why: the view out the bedroom window: a flat, painted backing two layers deep, already half-hazed so the vape only has to finish the job.

best_footage.element: a single chair facing an empty stairway under one ceiling light
best_footage.why: the room after he leaves it: a single object left in a lit box. Use as the composition for the bedroom's held wide.

best_footage.element: a tower facade receding into near-solid orange haze
best_footage.why: the film cut already uses it for this poem; take only its gradient logic (detail dissolving into flat haze toward the vanishing point) for the left-to-right haze claim, re-tinted teal.

insights: The EX works because he is a back: one back-of-head card, the bomber's silhouette and the ember carry him. Do not build him a face.
The haze must replace, not dim: paint it opaque and reveal it in a sweeping mask, the way the halfworld swaps dot allegiance. A cross-fade reads as a lighting cue, not a substance.
Put the window on a slider. The single gag of the poem is a destination that recedes; it is cheaper and stronger than any camera move.
In the fall keep the towers at mid value and the bodies at full ink; when the towers had full contrast the fall became wallpaper.
Shoot the party extras soft and on 4s and POET hard and on 2s: the slow motion is the difference between them.
End on the ember alone for a held beat; it is the hand-off to 02's flashing lights.
future: The black-tshirt POET pack and his falling cards serve 02 (floating in the black void).
The EX's back-only pack, now proven, carries him through 02, 03, 07, 08, 09.
The tower-strip belt returns for 02's road and 05's ascent.
The vintage party set and couples come back in 14.
The blue ember is the first appearance of the suite accent; 04 gives it to the heart.
